newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex ends firmer after dull session.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex ends firmer after dull session.

text.p: NYMEX crude oil futures prices ended slightly higher Monday, with refined products also posting mild gains, after a non-eventful, lightly traded session.
Crude oil for July delivery on the New York Mercantile Exchange rose 10 cents to settle at $20.98 a barrel, after trading in a range between $21.17 and $20.83.
July unleaded gasoline gained 0.18 cent to end at 62.99 cents a gallon. July heating oil settled at 56.32 cents a gallon, up 0.48 cent.
Traders said the markets were lifeless from start to finish during Monday's session, trading meekly on technical factors because they lack supply-and-demand fundamentals.
"There really just isn't much out there for direction, so the market may tend to trend sideways" in the near future, said Refco Inc analyst Victor Yu.
A brief move up early in the day found a small batch of speculator buy orders in July crude beginning at $21.10, but the upside break was short-lived, floor traders said.

As expected, United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan recommended Monday that the Iraqi oil-for-food accord, which allows Iraq to sell about $2.0 billion worth of oil to pay for food and other humanitarian supplies, be extended in its current form for another six months.
The full Security Council is expected to rule on the deal before it expires June 7.
"I think pretty much everyone expected a renewal, so there was no real suprpise there. I don't think much was put on it in the first place," Yu said.
Reviewing other fundamentals, Yu said the upcoming June 25 OPEC meeting should result in a renewal of the current oil sales terms.
"Gasoline season is underway and demand is good, but supply matches demand pretty well," he said.

Yu and other traders predicted the crude market would keep to a roughly one-dollar range between $20.50 and $21.50, basis July, for the short term, barring any significant news such as refinery outages.
